div.ab: CVII. Gif gesiðcund mon fare, ðonne mot he habban his gerefan mid him ⁊ his smið ⁊ his cildfestran.
CVII. Gif gesiðcund mon fare, þonne mot he habban his gerefan mid him ⁊ his smið ⁊ his cildfestran.
Si homo siþcundus abeat (transmigret), liceat ei habere prepositum suum (socios suos) secum et fabrum et nutricem suam.
{CVII} Gif gesiðcunde mon fare, þonne mot he habban his gerefan mid him ⁊ his smið ⁊ his cildfestran.
If a noble man moves [to a different district], he may take with him his reeve and his smith and his children’s nurse.
If a nobleman moves his residence he may take with him his reeve, his smith, and his children's nurse.
If a gesith-born man moves elsewhere, he may then have with him his reeve and his smith and his children’s nurse.
Wenn ein Mann vom Gefolgsadel [aus dem Lehngut] abzieht, dann darf er seinen Amtmann und seinen Schmied und seine Kinderamme mit sich nehmen.
If a man of the retainer nobility moves away [from his estate], then he may take his reeve and his smith and his children’s nurse with him.

note.quote: In Æthelberht §13 [L7] the king's smith is awarded "an ordinary person-price" of 100 shillings.
